chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Boyd Raeburn as a saxophonist
summary: Handy found Boyd a horrible saxophonist who played every reed instrument for show.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: To add my aside to this, in this project I've talked to twenty five, thirty guys from the band, at one time or another

had some relationship to the band, he's been described to me as the sweetest guy in the world, biggest schmuck, the biggest son of a bitch and everything in between. He's been described as a good saxophone player--
Oh, no, who could have described him as that?
I don't remember. Steve Jordan, I think talked of him as a good saxophone player.
Steve Jordan? Who is Steve Jordan?
Guitar player. Steve lives in Washington now. He was on one of the early bands.

I can't believe that anybody in this world that heard Boyd play saxophone could consider him a good saxophone player. In terms of the best to the worst, if he wasn't the worst, he was living the guy a hell of a run for the slot. He was a horrible saxophone player.
Could he read? Did he play the lines and play the notes?

He read fairly well. He could play the notes and he certainly made an attempt to play every reed instrument there was, because he had them standing up in front of the band; that I think was done to impress whoever was looking at the band.
It's a hell of a cover, a liner.

He was cute too. He would stand on this box in order to reach the mouthpiece of the bass saxophone he played. The instrument was bigger than he was. He was a tiny guy, a good looking guy but he didn't know a damn thing about music or what a band should sound like. He didn't know anything. I don't know how he became a bandleader, I don't know what his beginnings were.
I understand he had a society band.
